```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

[Neuroglancer](https://github.com/google/neuroglancer) keeps everything it
shows (layers, selected segments, camera position, layout and so on) in a
JSON *state*, usually encoded in the URL. nglscenes reads, builds and edits
these states from R.

```{r setup}
library(nglscenes)
```

## Scenes and layers are lists

A scene is the neuroglancer state as a named list with class `ngs_scene`, and
each layer is the layer's state with a class such as `ngs_segmentation_layer`.
You can read and set fields with `$` and `[[` like with any other list:

```{r}
sc <- ngs_scene(
  ngs_image_layer("precomputed://gs://neuroglancer-fafb-data/fafb_v14/fafb_v14_clahe",
                  name = "em"),
  ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://fafb-ffn1-20200412/segmentation",
                         name = "ffn1", segments = c(710435991, 2803641208)),
  layout = "3d"
)
sc

sc$layout
sc$layout <- "xy-3d"
sc$position <- c(109357, 41309, 5417)
```

All functions return a modified copy rather than changing the scene in place,
so they work well with pipes.

## Writing scenes

`ngs_url()` encodes the state in a URL for the scene's neuroglancer instance:

```{r}
url <- ngs_url(sc)
substr(url, 1, 120)
```

`ngs_open()` opens that URL in the browser, `ngs_to_clipboard()` copies it,
and `ngs_to_json()` / `ngs_to_file()` give you the JSON instead.

To use a different neuroglancer instance, change the base URL:

```{r}
ngs_base_url(sc) <- "https://spelunker.cave-explorer.org/"
substr(ngs_url(sc), 1, 60)
```

## Reading scenes

Scenes can be read from URLs (`ngs_from_url()`), JSON strings or state lists
(`ngs_from_string()`, `ngs_from_list()`), files (`ngs_from_file()`) and the
clipboard (`ngs_from_clipboard()`). URLs that point to a state server
(`?json_url=...`, `#!gs://...`, `#!middleauth+https://...`) are fetched
automatically.

```{r}
sc2 <- ngs_from_url(url)
sc2
```

Parsed scenes round-trip unchanged: writing a scene you have read gives the
same state back, including fields nglscenes doesn't know about.

```{r}
identical(ngs_to_json(sc2), ngs_to_json(ngs_from_url(ngs_url(sc2))))
```

## Managing layers

Layers are referred to by name or by (1-based) position:

```{r}
ngs_layer_names(sc)

sc <- sc |>
  ngs_add_layers(ngs_annotation_layer(name = "points")) |>
  ngs_move_layer("points", 1)
ngs_layer_names(sc)

ngs_layer(sc, "em")$visible <- FALSE
sc <- ngs_drop_layer(sc, "points")
```

Layer names must be unique within a scene: adding a layer whose name is
taken adds a suffix (e.g. `"ffn1-2"`).

## Segments and colours

Segment IDs are 64-bit integers, which R can't represent exactly as numbers.
nglscenes therefore always stores them as character, and converts numbers
(or `bit64::integer64` values) when they are set:

```{r}
ngs_segments(sc)
```

The helpers for segmentation layers accept a layer or a scene. With a scene,
`layer` picks the layer, or can be left out if there is only one
segmentation layer:

```{r}
sc <- sc |>
  ngs_add_segments(c("2803641209", "2803641210")) |>
  ngs_color_by(c("KC", "PN", "PN", "KC"), palette = "Okabe-Ito")

unlist(ngs_layer(sc, "ffn1")$segmentColors)
```

`ngs_set_colors()` sets colours directly, from a single colour, one colour per
segment or colours named by segment ID:

```{r}
sc <- ngs_set_colors(sc, c("710435991" = "red"), layer = "ffn1")
```

## Annotations

```{r}
an <- ngs_annotation_layer(name = "somata") |>
  ngs_add_points(data.frame(id = c("a", "b"),
                            x = c(1000, 2000), y = c(500, 600), z = c(10, 20)))
as.data.frame(an)
```

## Combining scenes

`+` adds all layers of the second scene to the first, and `|` merges layers
that share a source (e.g. combines the segments of two segmentation layers)
and adds the rest:

```{r}
a <- ngs_scene(ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://x/seg", segments = 1:2))
b <- ngs_scene(ngs_segmentation_layer("precomputed://gs://x/seg", segments = 2:3))

length((a + b)$layers)
ngs_segments(a | b)
```

## Graphene (CAVE) layers

Mainline neuroglancer and Spelunker spell CAVE chunkedgraph layers
differently from the Seung-lab fork (e.g. ngl.flywire.ai), and each refuses
the other's spelling. `ngs_for_viewer()` converts all graphene layers in a
scene:

```{r}
fw <- ngs_scene(ngs_flywire_layer(segments = "720575940621039145"))
fw$layers[[1]]$type

fw2 <- ngs_for_viewer(fw, "seunglab")
fw2$layers[[1]]$type
fw2$layers[[1]]$source
```

Fetching scenes from CAVE state servers requires a token, see
`?ngs_cave_token`.

## Segment properties

Segment properties add labels and searchable tags to segments. Create them
from a data frame and write them to an `info` file next to your
segmentation:

```{r}
props <- ngs_properties_from_df(data.frame(
  id = c(1, 2, 3),
  name = c("DA1_lPN", "DA1_lPN", "KCg-m"),
  class = factor(c("PN", "PN", "KC")),
  size = c(10.5, 12, 3)
))
props
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ngs_write_info(props, "segment_properties/info")
```
